chapter: Blackbirds, Carmen Jones and the Ziegfeld Follies
title: No influences: always aiming to be different
summary: He lists Lafayette comics and says nobody influenced him; he always aimed to surpass others and be only himself.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: We had Sandy (Markham) Burns, the comedian. We had Pig Meat Malcolm, comedian. We had Barlow, which is Sam Russell. We had Baby Cox -- and what is her name --
Did any of these people in particular impress you or have an influence on you or change your attitude towards your own work or your own comedy or give you ideas?
I find it hard to believe that no other act, no other musician and no other singer, no other comic had any influence on you in some way or another.
To what extent? To the kind that you admired that you perhaps emulated in some way even borrowed or adopted some of the things that they did into your own act.
No, man, I'm sorry I can't find nothing. I wish I could, I'd love to tell ya.

I have to beat 'em, man. Look, I'm coming out of that room and I enter this room -- that's the idea. Coming out of that room into this room in here, understand? I've got to find this room is going to be different from that room over there. Then I've got to be as different in here as I was over there, for this room -- that's the same difference I learned to act, that's the same way. I run into an actor, singer or dancer, I don't care who it is, I've got to be different from what they are so I've got to greet them with the same idea

that I had coming out of that room into this one, the same way. And there's nothing they have that I wanted to be any part of what I want to do. Because what I'm going to do is going to surpass what they're doing. That was my idea in show business. I get something new that nobody can do but me, 'cause nobody know a thing about it but me. What George does, that's what he does. Let Sammy Davis impersonate all he wants to impersonate. Let him keep on. I just want to do me. Get my point? And I've been me all my life. I couldn't be nobody else but me. I tried to do steps like some other dancers, but you don't wind up nowhere. Steps don't mean nothing. Don't come out right. I do them but they don't come out right.
This is where we're at -- what show am I talking to you about?
